headline: Medium risk: shared-output workflows can create prompt-injection, leakage, and action-conflict issues between Argo Workflows and Rasa.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can emit artifacts and Rasa ingests text/voice messages through chat channels, so a workflow output could be copied into a bot conversation and treated as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, but the pair has plausible manual or API bridging, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF Argo outputs are pasted or forwarded into Rasa training or runtime messages
IF a shared Slack/Messenger/Twilio channel is used to relay workflow text into the bot
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation in forwarded messages
Require human review before copying workflow output into bot prompts
Strip executable-looking text from workflow artifacts before forwarding
Use a separate channel for machine output and user dialogue
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to messages end-to-end

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo touches artifacts and parameters, while Rasa handles text and voice; both have allowlisted egress, but no shared workspace or secret-handling is documented. The main leakage path is manual or integration-based transfer of sensitive artifacts into bot conversations, which is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF artifacts or parameters contain sensitive data and are forwarded into Rasa channels
IF either system is configured to log full message payloads externally
mitigations: Redact sensitive fields before forwarding outputs
Disable verbose conversation logging for sensitive channels
Limit bot inputs to non-sensitive summaries
Review allowlisted egress destinations for both systems
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at the integration boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo is a workflow engine and Rasa is a conversational bot framework; their documented surfaces do not show overlapping filesystem or OAuth writes, and Rasa cannot run multiple instances. A direct write-write conflict is not evidenced, so only a small coordination risk remains if both are wired to the same mutable backend.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external resource without locking
IF an integration maps both to the same mutable queue or database
mitigations: Assign separate resource namespaces
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Avoid shared mutable state where possible
Add optimistic-lock checks on shared records
requires-engineering: introduce explicit locking for shared backends

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo can produce workflow artifacts that Rasa may surface in dialogue, so downstream users could act on unverified workflow-derived content. There is no documented verification step between them, but no evidence that either agent autonomously executes high-impact actions from the other's output, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Rasa presents Argo-generated status or facts as authoritative to end users
IF downstream operators act on bot messages without independent verification
mitigations: Mark workflow-derived messages as unverified
Add a confirmation step before any action based on bot output
Require source links in user-facing summaries
Train Rasa to ask clarifying questions on uncertain workflow results
requires-engineering: add validation against the workflow source of truth

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only open-source systems with no stated residency, certification, or retention commitments, so a concrete compliance breach is not established. The only plausible issue is policy mismatch if sensitive data from Argo artifacts is routed through Rasa channels with different logging or retention settings.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Rasa channels with longer retention than Argo artifacts
IF deployment policies assign different residency or logging rules to the two systems
mitigations: Document retention for both systems
Avoid sending regulated data through chat channels
Align log retention settings
Review deployment residency for each service
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
